questions.q: What does curl show that ping cannot?
options: The actual HTTP response — status code, headers, and body — from the application
Which router hops a packet passes through
The DNS record for a domain
questions.explain: curl makes a real HTTP request and shows the application's actual response, unlike ping which only tests ICMP reachability.

questions.q: What does an HTTP 500 status code indicate?
options: The server hit an internal error while handling a request it did receive
The connection was refused before reaching the application
questions.explain: A 500 means the server received the request but encountered an internal error while processing it.

questions.q: What do netstat and ss show on a server?
options: The DNS records for the server's domain
Which ports are listening and which connections are currently open
The path traffic takes from a remote client
questions.explain: netstat and ss report locally which ports a machine is listening on and which connections are active.

questions.q: Which tool is the modern, typically faster replacement for the other on current Linux systems?
questions.explain: ss is the modern replacement for the older netstat command, producing similar output more efficiently.

questions.q: A server responds to ping but refuses connections to its application port. What does this most likely indicate?
options: Nothing is listening on that port, or a local rule is blocking it
questions.explain: Reachability at the ICMP level doesn't guarantee the application port is bound or reachable; ss on the server can confirm whether anything is actually listening there.
